text:
anna: flagging a perf regression after yesterday's authz move. dataset-heavy dashboards have 95p tail up ~130ms. noticed mostly on tenants with many small panels

ravi: saw that too. traces show authz calls exploding due to per-panel lookups. prefilter at gateway was removed in the refactor and replaced by per-query sidecar checks

chris: can you paste a trace snippet? is it repeated auth calls or retries?

anna: snippet: \nquery(panelA)->authz-sidecar(check resource)->query-db\nquery(panelB)->authz-sidecar(check resource)->query-db\n... (10 panels)\nWe now do N auth calls per dashboard render instead of 1

lee: TL;DR: correctness vs volume. New model is principled (fine-grained) but multiplies RPCs. We need a mitigation path that preserves correctness for sensitive tenants

sam: brainstorm options:
- revert to gateway-prefilter (quick, coarse)
- batch authz API (server change, long-term)
- client-side microcache + tenant-aware warmup (fast)
- hybrid routing: gateway-prefilter for identified panel-types + sidecar for others

ravi: +1 batching long-term. For short-term we can combine client microcache + request coalescing in sidecar to reduce duplicate inflight requests

chris: microcache design constraints: per-tenant entries, TTL tuned to 10-30s, eviction policy LRU with size caps, and stats for misses. Need to avoid stale allow/deny causing exposures

lee: security note: any cached allow must be conservative. prefer caching denials for shorter TTL than allows. Also log audit events for cache hits on sensitive resources

anna: impact goal: keep panel 99p < 350ms. Current 99p ~420ms for heavy dashboards. Also watch auth error rate spike (should be zero)

sam: sample API for batching (ops sketch):
POST /v1/authz/batch
{ tenant_id: "t-123", action: "view", resources: [{type: "panel", id: "p1"}, {type: "panel", id: "p2"}] }
returns: { "p1": "allow", "p2": "deny" }

ravi: implementation notes: server should accept mixed resource types, support streaming responses for very large batches, and expose per-resource eval time in trace

chris: rollout plan proposal:
1) enable microcache + coalescing in sidecar for 100% (small change)
2) gateway-prefilter toggle for top-10 heavy dashboards (controlled toggle, rollbackable)
3) implement batched API and deploy as canary (5%)
4) switch clients to batch + fallback to single-call sidecar

lee: metrics and gates: monitor panel render 95p/99p, auth sidecar 95p, and permission mismatch rate (should be 0). Add an SLO alert at 99p>350ms

anna: action items:
- ravi: prototype microcache+coalesce in sidecar (ETA 3d)
- sam: spec batched API + server perf targets (ETA 2w)
- chris: config toggle + canary playbook + dashboard (ETA 1d)
- lee: update security note and audit logging plan (ETA 2d)

infra-bot: deploy done: sidecar v2.3.1 -> canary=5%. Metric collection enabled

ravi: I'll push a micro-spike today to validate coalescing decreases duplicate calls. will post numbers here

sam: add a regression test vector to the eval harness that renders a 12-panel dashboard with mixed tenants so this shows up in CI

anna: thanks all. if microcache doesn't bring 95p within 300ms we will flip gateway-prefilter and prioritize batching work
